questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Consider the following in respect of inverse circular functions :
I. $\sin^{-1}(-x)=-\sin^{-1}x$
II. $\cos^{-1}(-x)=\cos^{-1}x$
III. $\tan^{-1}(-x)=\pi-\tan^{-1}x$
IV. $\cot^{-1}(-x)=\pi-\cot^{-1}x$
How many of the above are correct ?
questions.solution:
Statement I: $\sin^{-1}(-x) = -\sin^{-1}x$ is a standard property of inverse trigonometric functions and is correct.

Statement II: The correct property is $\cos^{-1}(-x) = \pi - \cos^{-1}x$. Hence, this statement is incorrect.

Statement III: The correct property is $\tan^{-1}(-x) = -\tan^{-1}x$. Hence, this statement is incorrect.

Statement IV: $\cot^{-1}(-x) = \pi - \cot^{-1}x$ is a standard property and is correct.

Exactly two of the given statements are correct.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\tan^{-1}k + \tan^{-1}\dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$, then what is the value of $k$?
questions.solution:
Given $\tan^{-1}k + \tan^{-1}\dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$

Using the formula $\tan^{-1}x + \tan^{-1}y = \tan^{-1} \left(\dfrac{x+y}{1-xy}\right), we get:

\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{k + \dfrac{1}{2}}{1 - \dfrac{k}{2}}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{4}

\dfrac{2k + 1}{2 - k} = \tan \left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)

\dfrac{2k + 1}{2 - k} =1$

$2k + 1 = 2 - k$

$3k = 1$

$k = \dfrac{1}{3}$

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{3}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is the value of $\tan \left[\dfrac{1}{2}\sec^{-1}  \left(\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\right)\right]?$
questions.solution:
Let $\theta = \sec^{-1} \left(\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\right)

\Rightarrow \sec \theta = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}

⇒ \theta = \dfrac{\pi}{6}

The given expression becomes \tan \left(\dfrac{1}{2} \theta\right) = \tan \left(\dfrac{\pi}{12}\right)

\tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{12}\right) = \tan(15^{{}^{\circ}}) = \tan(45^{{}^{\circ}} - 30^{{}^{\circ}})$

Using the formula $\tan(A - B) = \dfrac{\tan A - \tan B}{1 + \tan A \tan B}

\tan(15^{{}^{\circ}}) = \dfrac{\tan 45^{{}^{\circ}} - \tan 30^{{}^{\circ}}}{1 + \tan 45^{{}^{\circ}} \tan 30^{{}^{\circ}}}

\tan(15^{{}^{\circ}}) = \dfrac{1 - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}}{1 + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3} - 1}{\sqrt{3} + 1}

Rationalizing the denominator:

\tan(15^{{}^{\circ}}) = \dfrac{(\sqrt{3} - 1)^2}{(\sqrt{3} + 1)(\sqrt{3} - 1)} = \dfrac{3 + 1 - 2\sqrt{3}}{3 - 1}

\tan(15^{{}^{\circ}}) = \dfrac{4 - 2\sqrt{3}}{2} =2 - \sqrt{3}

Answer: 2 - \sqrt{3}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Consider the following for the two (02) items that follow:
Let $y = \sin^{-1}\left(x - \dfrac{4x^3}{27}\right)$.

What is $y$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Given $y = \sin^{-1}\left(x - \dfrac{4x^3}{27}\right)$

Substitute $x = 3\sin\theta$, which gives $\sin\theta = \dfrac{x}{3}$ or $\theta = \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right)$

The expression becomes:

$y = \sin^{-1}\left(3\sin\theta - \dfrac{4(3\sin\theta)^3}{27}\right)$

$y = \sin^{-1}\left(3\sin\theta - \dfrac{4(27\sin^3\theta)}{27}\right)$

$y = \sin^{-1}(3\sin\theta - 4\sin^3\theta)$

Using the trigonometric identity $\sin(3\theta) = 3\sin\theta - 4\sin^3\theta$:

$y = \sin^{-1}(\sin(3\theta))$

$y = 3\theta$

Substituting back the value of $\theta$:

$y = 3\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right)$

Answer: $3\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right)$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $k$ is a root of $x^2 - 4x + 1 = 0$, then what is $\tan^{-1}k + \tan^{-1}\dfrac{1}{k}$ equal to?
questions.solution:
The given equation is $x^2 - 4x + 1 = 0$.

The roots of the equation are given by $x = \dfrac{4 \pm \sqrt{16 - 4}}{2} = 2 \pm \sqrt{3}$.

Since $\sqrt{3} \approx 1.732$, both roots $2 + \sqrt{3}$ and $2 - \sqrt{3}$ are positive. Therefore, $k > 0$.

Using the standard inverse trigonometric identity for $x > 0$:

$\tan^{-1}x + \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

Substituting $x = k$, we get:

$\tan^{-1}k + \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{k}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

Answer: $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $\tan\left[2\tan^{-1}\dfrac{1}{2}-\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right]$ equal to ?
questions.solution:
Let $\theta = \tan^{-1}\dfrac{1}{2}$, which implies $\tan\theta = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

We need to evaluate $\tan\left(2\theta - \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$.

First, calculate $\tan(2\theta)$ using the double angle formula:

$\tan(2\theta) = \dfrac{2\tan\theta}{1 - \tan^2\theta} = \dfrac{2\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)}{1 - \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2} = \dfrac{1}{1 - \dfrac{1}{4}} = \dfrac{4}{3}$

Now, apply the tangent subtraction formula:

$\tan\left(2\theta - \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \dfrac{\tan(2\theta) - \tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)}{1 + \tan(2\theta)\tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)}$

Substitute $\tan(2\theta) = \dfrac{4}{3}$ and $\tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = 1$:

$\tan\left(2\theta - \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \dfrac{\dfrac{4}{3} - 1}{1 + \dfrac{4}{3}(1)} = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{3}}{\dfrac{7}{3}} = \dfrac{1}{7}$

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{7}$

questions.q: What is $\cot^{-1} 9 + \text{cosec}^{-1} \left(\dfrac{\sqrt{41}}{4}\right) equal to?  $
questions.solution:
Let $A = \cot^{-1} 9 \Rightarrow \cot A = 9 \Rightarrow \tan A = \dfrac{1}{9}$

Let $B = \text{cosec}^{-1}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{41}}{4}\right) \Rightarrow \text{cosec} B = \dfrac{\sqrt{41}}{4} \Rightarrow \sin B = \dfrac{4}{\sqrt{41}}$

From this, $\tan B = \dfrac{4}{\sqrt{(\sqrt{41})^2 - 4^2}} = \dfrac{4}{\sqrt{41 - 16}} = \dfrac{4}{5}$

Using the formula $\tan(A + B) = \dfrac{\tan A + \tan B}{1 - \tan A \tan B}$:

$\tan(A + B) = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{9} + \dfrac{4}{5}}{1 - \left(\dfrac{1}{9}\right)\left(\dfrac{4}{5}\right)}$

$\tan(A + B) = \dfrac{\dfrac{5 + 36}{45}}{\dfrac{45 - 4}{45}}$

$\tan(A + B) = \dfrac{41}{41} = 1$

Since $A, B \in \left(0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right), we have $A + B = $\dfrac{\pi}{4}$$

Answer: \dfrac{\pi}{4}$

questions.solution:
$\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{2 x+3 x}{1-2 x.3 x}\right)=\frac{\pi}{4}\begin{gathered}
\tan ^{-1} \frac{5 x}{1-6 x^2}=\frac{\pi}{4} \\
\frac{5 x}{1-6 x^2}=1 \\
1-6 x^2=5 x \\
6 x^2+5 x-1=0 \\
(6 x-1)(x+1)=0 \\
\Rightarrow x=\frac{1}{6},-1
\end{gathered}\Rightarrow \quad x=\frac{1}{6}$
Here $x=-1$ rejected.

2. \tan ^{-1} \sqrt{3}+\tan ^{-1} 1=-\tan ^{-1}(2+\sqrt{3})$

$\begin{aligned}
& \sin ^{-1} x+\sin ^{-1} y=\sin ^{-1}\left(x \sqrt{1-y^2}+y \sqrt{1-x^2}\right) \\
& \text{ If }(-1 \leq x, y \leq 1) \&\left(x^2+y^2 \leq 1\right) \\
& \Rightarrow \sin ^{-1}\left(\frac{4}{5}\right)+\sin ^{-1} \frac{3}{5} \\
& =\sin ^{-1}\left[\frac{4}{5} \sqrt{1-\left(\frac{3}{5}\right)^2}+\frac{3}{5} \sqrt{1-\left(\frac{4}{5}\right)^2}\right] \\
& =\sin ^{-1}\left[\frac{16}{25}+\frac{9}{25}\right] \\
& =\sin ^{-1}(1)=\frac{\pi}{2}
\end{aligned}\therefore$ Statement (1) is correct
Again-
$\begin{aligned}
& \tan ^{-1} x+\tan ^{-1} y=\pi+\tan ^{-1}\left[\frac{x+y}{1-x y}\right] \\
& \operatorname{If} ;(x > 0),(y > 0) \text{$ and $}(x y > 1) \\
& \tan ^{-1}(\sqrt{3})+\tan ^{-1}(1)=\pi+\tan ^{-1}\left[\frac{\sqrt{3}+1}{1-\sqrt{3}}\right] \\
& =\pi+\tan ^{-1}\left[\frac{(\sqrt{3}+1)(1+\sqrt{3})}{(1-\sqrt{3})(1+\sqrt{3})}\right]
\end{aligned}\begin{aligned}
& =\pi+\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{4+2 \sqrt{3}}{-2}\right) \\
& =\pi+\tan ^{-1}[-(2+\sqrt{3})] \\
& =\pi-\tan ^{-1}(2+\sqrt{3}) \quad \because \tan ^{-1}(-x)=-\tan ^{-1} x
\end{aligned}\therefore$ Statement (1) is incorrect.

questions.q:
What is the value of
$\cos \left\{\cos ^{-1} \frac{4}{5}+\cos ^{-1} \frac{12}{13}\right\} ?$
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \text{ Put } \cos ^{-1} \frac{4}{5}=\mathrm{A} \\
& \cos \mathrm{ A}=\frac{4}{5} \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \sin \mathrm{ A}=\frac{3}{5} \\
& \cos ^{-1} \frac{12}{13}=\mathrm{B} \\
& \cos \mathrm{ B}=\frac{12}{13} \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \sin \mathrm{ B}=\frac{5}{13} \text{. } \\
& \text{ Now, } \\
& \cos \left(\cos ^{-1} \frac{4}{5}+\cos ^{-1} \frac{12}{13}\right) \\
& =\cos (\mathrm{A}+\mathrm{B}) \\
& =\cos \mathrm{A} \cos \mathrm{ B}-\sin \mathrm{A} \sin \mathrm{ B} \\
& =\left(\frac{4}{5}\right)\left(\frac{12}{13}\right)-\left(\frac{3}{5}\right)\left(\frac{5}{13}\right) \\
& =\frac{48}{65}-\frac{15}{65}=\frac{33}{65}.
\end{aligned}$
